newsitem.title: ITALY: Isco sees Italy rates falling to help deficit.
newsitem.headline: Isco sees Italy rates falling to help deficit.

text.p: Italy's state budget deficit will come in at three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997 thanks in part to a further expected fall in interest rates, state-funded economic research institute Isco said.
Isco economist Giovanni Palmieri told a parliamentary hearing that the 1997 budget would have to be extremely effective if the three percent goal was to be reached.

In addition, Isco was expecting "a further, gradual fall in interest rates that will bring around a half point reduction in yields on annual short term bills between now and the end of the year," Palmieri said.
This would help cut Italy's huge debt servicing costs.
The government has pledged to hit the three percent target this year to meet a key requirement of the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to sign up to the single European currency.
Italy's deficit/GDP ratio was 6.7 percent in 1996. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
